quotes.text: In Azure Foundry, a thread isn't a casual chat window that evaporates when you close it. It's a persistent conversation session.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear definition of a thread in Foundry agents.

quotes.text: A run is the trigger that activates the agent to take that context and actually execute on it.

quotes.text: With run steps, you can scroll through the timeline, identify the exact misfire, and patch it. Debugging stops being guesswork and becomes forensics.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows the practical debugging value of run steps.

takeaways: An Azure AI Foundry agent combines a model, instructions and tools, which gives you reproducible and auditable behaviour instead of loose text generation.
Threads keep a persistent, time-stamped conversation record, runs execute the agent on that thread, and run steps log every tool call and message for debugging and audits.
Built-in tools, OpenAPI and MCP extensions and Logic Apps connectors widen what agents can do, while on-behalf-of authentication keeps user permissions intact.
hook: When an AI agent gives a wrong answer, can you prove how it got there? This episode is for developers and compliance teams working with Azure AI Foundry and explains how threads, runs and run steps create an auditable trail of every message and tool call, so agents become traceable, debuggable and ready for enterprise use.
